definitions.explanation: An expression of dissatisfaction or annoyance.

examples.japanese: {文句|もんく}ばかり{言|い}わないで。
この{仕事|しごと}に{文句|もんく}はないが、{給料|きゅうりょう}にはちょっと{不満|ふまん}がある。
examples.english: I have no complaints about this job, but I'm a little dissatisfied with the salary.

examples.japanese: {決|き}まり{文句|もんく}を{覚|おぼ}えると{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: It's convenient to memorize set phrases.
examples.notes: 決まり文句 = set phrase, stock phrase

examples.japanese: あの{歌|うた}の{文句|もんく}がなかなか{思|おも}い{出|だ}せない。
examples.english: I just can't remember the words to that song.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{殺|ころ}し{文句|もんく}に{思|おも}わず{笑|わら}ってしまった。
examples.english: I couldn't help but laugh at his killer line.
examples.notes: 殺し文句 = killer line, winning phrase

notes:
USAGE: {文句|もんく} is commonly used to mean "complaint" in casual speech. It's less formal than {苦情|くじょう}.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{文句|もんく}を{言|い}う (to complain)
・{文句|もんく}がある (to have a complaint)
・{文句|もんく}なし (no complaints, perfect)
・{決|き}まり{文句|もんく} (set phrase)
・{殺|ころ}し{文句|もんく} (killer line, winning phrase)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{苦情|くじょう} - complaint (formal)
・{不平|ふへい} - complaint, discontent
・{不満|ふまん} - dissatisfaction
